Why go: a slow day on a classic wooden junk

The Red Baron is a 30 m junk built from ironwood in a Surat Thani yard, with red sails, a sun deck with loungers, a covered saloon and two toilets. It moves at about 6 knots, so the day is about the journey: eating, swimming off the side and watching the islands go by rather than racing between stops.

The sunset dinner cruise is the easiest way in: three hours, a swim stop at Koh Som and a buffet dinner as the light goes. The day cruises suit people who want space on deck and a full meal rather than the bounce of a speedboat.

Which cruise to choose

The sunset dinner cruise is the best value and the easiest to fit into a holiday: three hours, a swim stop at Koh Som and a Thai buffet. The Koh Phangan day adds swimming, snorkelling or fishing and a buffet lunch before an afternoon cruise along the coast. The Ang Thong day is the longest, with breakfast, snorkelling, lunch and either the Emerald Lake or the Koh Wua Talab viewpoint; because the junk is slow, it suits people who enjoy time at sea as much as time ashore.

Who it suits

  • Couples and families who prefer a stable, spacious boat to a speedboat.
  • Older travellers and anyone who dislikes fast boats.
  • Guests who want a sunset cruise at a shared-tour price.

Who should choose something else

  • Anyone who wants maximum time at Ang Thong: the junk is slow, so a speedboat day tour spends more time in the park.
  • Groups wanting the whole boat: see the Red Baron private charter.

Good to know

  • Set days: book the cruise that runs on your date; we confirm by email or WhatsApp.
  • Ang Thong season: the park reopens on 16 December.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time.
